==Problem==
Isabella has <imath>6</imath> coupons that can be redeemed for free ice cream cones at Pete's Sweet Treats. In order to make the coupons last, she decides that she will redeem one every <imath>10</imath> days until she has used them all. She knows that Pete's is closed on Sundays, but as she circles the <imath>6</imath> dates on her calendar, she realizes that no circled date falls on a Sunday.  On what day of the week does Isabella redeem her first coupon?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }\text{Monday}\qquad\textbf{(B) }\text{Tuesday}\qquad\textbf{(C) }\text{Wednesday}\qquad\textbf{(D) }\text{Thursday}\qquad\textbf{(E) }\text{Friday}</imath>

==Solution 1 ( Guess and Check! )==
Let <imath>\text{Day
}1</imath> to <imath>\text{Day\\ }2</imath> denote a day where one coupon is redeemed and the day when the second coupon is redeemed. 

If she starts on a <imath>\text{Monday}</imath>, she redeems her next coupon on <imath>\text{Thursday}</imath>. 

<imath>\text{Thursday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Sunday}</imath>.

Thus, <imath>\textbf{(A)}\ \text{Monday}</imath> is incorrect.


If she starts on a <imath>\text{Tuesday}</imath>, she redeems her next coupon on <imath>\text{Friday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Friday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Monday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Monday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Thursday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Thursday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Sunday}</imath>.

Thus <imath>\textbf{(B)}\ \text{Tuesday}</imath> is incorrect.


If she starts on a <imath>\text{Wednesday}</imath>, she redeems her next coupon on <imath>\text{Saturday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Saturday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Tuesday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Tuesday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Friday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Friday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Monday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Monday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Thursday}</imath>.

And on <imath>\text{Thursday}</imath>, she redeems her last coupon. 


No Sunday occured; thus, <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ \text{Wednesday}}</imath> is correct. 


Checking for the other options, 


If she starts on a <imath>\text{Thursday}</imath>, she redeems her next coupon on <imath>\text{Sunday}</imath>.

Thus, <imath>\textbf{(D)}\ \text{Thursday}</imath> is incorrect.


If she starts on a <imath>\text{Friday}</imath>, she redeems her next coupon on <imath>\text{Monday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Monday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Thursday}</imath>.

<imath>\text{Thursday}</imath> to <imath>\text{Sunday}</imath>.


Checking for the other options gave us negative results; thus, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ \text{Wednesday}}</imath>.

~KangarooPrecise and ( ??? )

== Solution 2 ==
Let the days of the week be numbers<imath>\pmod 7</imath>. <imath>3</imath> and <imath>7</imath> are coprime, so continuously adding <imath>3</imath> to a number<imath>\pmod 7</imath> will cycle through all numbers from <imath>0</imath> to <imath>6</imath>. If a string of 6 numbers in this cycle does not contain <imath>0</imath>, then if you minus 3 from the first number of this cycle, it will always be <imath>0</imath>. So, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C) Wednesday}}</imath>.

~~SmileKat32

== Solution 3 ==
Start counting on Sunday, to maximize the number of 10-day jumps before reaching Sunday again. Add the 10 (<imath>\equiv 3 \pmod 7</imath>) days to reach the first coupon day on <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)\ Wednesday}}</imath>.

~~ gorefeebuddie

Note: This only works when 7 and 3 are relatively prime. Otherwise, you’d prefer to start on a day whose distance from Sunday is relatively prime to the jump size.

== Solution 4 ==
Let Sunday be Day 0, Monday be Day 1, Tuesday be Day 2, and so forth. We see that Sundays fall on Day <imath>n</imath>, where n is a multiple of seven. If Isabella starts using her coupons on Monday (Day 1), she will fall on a Day that is a multiple of seven, a Sunday (her third coupon will be "used" on Day 21). Similarly, if she starts using her coupons on Tuesday (Day 2), Isabella will fall on a Day that is a multiple of seven (Day 42). Repeating this process, if she starts on Wednesday (Day 3), Isabella will first fall on a Day that is a multiple of seven, Day 63 (13, 23, 33, 43, 53 are not multiples of seven), but on her seventh coupon, of which she only has six. So, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\text{ Wednesday}}</imath>.


== Solution 5 ==
There is a ten day gap, so every time you are 3 days ahead. For Sunday to be the 7th day you must be 6 days ahead, so 6x3 = 18. 18 days prior is the same as 4 days prior to Sunday which is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\text{ Wednesday}}</imath>.
